question.text: White light is passed through a double slit and interference is observed on a screen <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> away. The separation between the slits is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The first violet and red fringes are formed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> away from the central white fringes. The difference in wavelengths of red and violet light is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mtext>in</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
y1=λrDd

y2=λvDd

λr−λv=y1−y2dD=(3.5−2)mm×0.3mm1.5m=300nm
